title: The Door to the Pass
hook: Hold eastbound. She is not cleared for the pass.
scene: Clear cold morning on a two-lane street at the last downtown block, heading east. The Menace is STOPPED in the eastbound travel lane at the painted stop line — the last downtown crosswalk edge — on wet asphalt between the lane paint and the right curb. Wheels are still. A pedestrian is stepping off the curb into that marked crosswalk ahead of the plow; that is why she holds. The full-width nose plow sits on the front bull bar and points east. Behind the car, west, brick downtown blocks line the left third of this same street. Ahead, east, the same two-lane continues with wet paint and no other playable vehicles. Both cats are a sound in the closed carrier on the floor. Hold. You are not cleared for the pass.
debrief: Downtown sits behind the Beetle. She is stopped at the last crosswalk. She is not cleared for the pass.

source.teaching_target: Hold the eastbound at the last downtown stop line; a pedestrian stepping off the curb is why she is not cleared; city on the left shares that street; empty eastbound continues right.

image_brief.camera_pose: Shallower high-oblique aerial photograph, about forty degrees off vertical, looking along a wet two-lane street that crosses the full frame from the left edge to the right edge so the pavement has readable depth. Not map-flat top-down. Not eye-level. Not a three-quarter front portrait. The Beetle is a small mass in the lower half of the frame.

image_brief.read: the Beetle is stopped at the last downtown crosswalk holding eastbound; a pedestrian stepping off the curb is why she is not cleared for the pass; downtown shares that street on the left
